decision: Queue on the left, one return worked at a time on the right, in three numbered steps
why: A return happens with the customer standing at the counter; receipt → condition → refund is the order staff actually do it in, and numbering it makes the next step obvious on a tablet.
alternative: A single long form with every field visible at once.
value: Fewer skipped checks and a refund in under a minute without training.

decision: Refunding to Maré Pay reverses installments instead of refunding the full price
why: The customer has only paid one of three installments; canceling the remaining ones and returning what was paid is the only outcome that never over- or under-refunds (refundQuote is unit-tested).
alternative: Refund the full amount to the card on file and let collections reconcile it.
value: Money is right the first time, and the customer's statement tells the same story as the receipt.

decision: Store credit +10% is pre-selected and labeled Recommended, but every option stays one tap away
why: Retention matters to the business, yet steering must never hide the customer's legal right to the original payment.
alternative: Ask the staff member to pitch store credit verbally.
value: A consistent, honest nudge; the option mix shows up in the KPI row as it changes.

decision: Confirming emits returns.refunded through the outbox; Circle and Mesh react to the event
why: Counter should not call Circle's commission API directly: the reversal must happen even if Circle is down, exactly once, with the return id as the idempotency key.
alternative: Synchronous calls from the store portal to Pay, Circle and invoicing.
value: The creator's commission is reversed while still inside the 30-day window, and Mesh shows the event with its key.

decision: New returns arrive from the in-browser world simulation, not a backend
why: The queue must feel live for every reviewer, but a server or database per viewer would cost money and fail when the free tier sleeps.
alternative: Poll a Supabase table every few seconds.
value: The demo costs $0, works offline, and every tab shows the same returns because the world is seeded.

decision: The receipt scan runs on the tablet and only the matched order id leaves it
why: Receipts and app screens can show personal data; the counter only needs the order reference.
alternative: Upload the photo for server-side OCR.
value: Less personal data in transit and a scan that still works when the store is offline.
